topic: Weekend sleep-ins and Sunday bedtime (1-6 years)
video_title: Sleeps in on weekends? Fix Sunday bedtime calmly (ages 1-6)

slides.text:
Your child sleeps in on weekends, and by Sunday bedtime keeps getting later and later.

**Here's a calm way to reset it.**
slides.voiceover: Sleeps in on weekends? Here's a calm reset.

slides.text:
If Sunday bedtime is a mess, it's rarely your child's fault, and rarely yours.

Weekends bend the schedule for everyone. **Small steps** bring it back, no strict rules needed. (Ages 1-6 years)
slides.voiceover: Weekends bend the schedule. Small steps help.

slides.text:
**1. Keep the wake-up time close.**

The AAP says the same waking time on weekdays and weekends, with regular meals, nap and play times, helps children feel secure and bedtime go smoothly.
slides.voiceover: Step one. Keep the wake-up time close.

slides.text:
**2. Open the curtains right away.**

The AAP suggests bright light when it's time to get up, to help stimulate wakefulness. Even on a lazy Saturday.
slides.voiceover: Step two. Open the curtains right away.

slides.text:
**3. Get outside in daylight.**

The AAP says sunlight has a strong effect on the body's circadian rhythm, so time outdoors helps the body clock settle. A morning walk counts.
slides.voiceover: Step three. Get outside in daylight.

slides.text:
**4. Start bedtime a little earlier.**

The AAP suggests starting before your child shows signs of tiredness. Even 15 to 20 minutes earlier can make a big difference.
slides.voiceover: Step four. Start bedtime fifteen to twenty minutes earlier.

slides.text:
**Try saying on Saturday morning:**

"Good morning! Let's open the curtains and see the sun."

Then stay close to the usual wake-up time. **Calm and steady** wins.
slides.voiceover: Say: Good morning! Let's open the curtains.

caption:
"Sleeps in on weekends, and Sunday bedtime is a mess." Sound familiar? 💤
A few calm steps can help: a wake-up time close to your weekday one, bright light and daylight in the morning, and bedtime 15-20 minutes earlier (ages 1-6 years).
Save this and send it to a co-parent before the weekend.
